pencereler.0-5: Qantas Flight 32 suffered an uncontained engine failure. In seconds, debris tore through the
pencereler.5-12: wing and cut wiring. The crew spent nearly two hours working through failures, then landed safely. The cause was
pencereler.12-20: a small oil pipe inside the engine. It had been machined off-centre, leaving its wall too thin. A fatigue crack leaked oil,
pencereler.20-30: which caught fire. A turbine disc overheated and burst. Engines with the faulty pipe were inspected and replaced.

segmentler.metin: Qantas Flight 32 suffered an uncontained engine failure.
It took only a fatigue crack in an oil pipe made with a thin wall.
So how could a fatigue crack in an oil pipe made with a thin wall do this?
The answer is misaligned counterbore thinning an oil feed stub pipe, leading to fatigue, oil fire and turbine disc failure — and it is why engines with the faulty pipe were inspected and replaced.
